title: Registry: datastore failover is a DR operation (graceful, actionable)
description: Runs `nexus failover-test cluster registry --direction registry-db --yes`. The adapter performs the VRRP cutover (stop keepalived on the .119 holder; the peer promotes PG + re-masters Redis via the keepalived notify scripts) and measures the RTO — but the keepalived demote.sh re-attaches Redis only, NOT PostgreSQL, so the demoted node stays a second PG primary (split-brain by design, like the lakehouse iceberg-pg pair). A real registry-db failover is therefore a DR runbook (promote + fence + pg_basebackup re-seed of the old primary). Live execution was deferred at v0.8.5 to avoid degrading the freshly-rebuilt datastore; the app tier needs no VIP (RR DNS, clients retry).

observe.what: VIP moves to the peer + PG promotes there + Redis re-masters (RTO measured); the recovery hint notes the old primary must re-sync as a PG standby via pg_basebackup — the DR step demote.sh does not auto-do
the app pair has no VIP — an actionable N/A routing the operator to --direction registry-db

whatProves: RegistryAdapter.FailoverAsync drives the registry-db VRRP cutover (VIP move + PG promote + Redis re-master) and reports the RTO; it refuses an app-tier "failover" (RR-DNS, no VIP). The PG re-attach of the demoted primary is a documented DR re-seed, mirroring lakehouse iceberg-pg.
